chunks: Safwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the ḥamīl, and he said: “And what thing is the ḥamīl?”

So I said: A woman is taken captive from her land, with her young child with her, and she says, “He is my son.” And a man is taken captive and meets his brother, and he says, “He is my brother.” They have no proof except their own statement.
He said: “What do the people among you say about it?” I said: They do not allow him to inherit when they do not have proof of his birth; rather, his birth had occurred in shirk.

He said: “Glory be to Allah! If she comes with her son, she has continued acknowledging him as such; and if he recognizes his brother, and that was in a state of soundness from both of them, then they have continued acknowledging that, and some of them inherit from others.”

key_terms.الْحَمِيلُ: a captive relative whose lineage or kinship is being claimed
key_terms.فِي الشِّرْكِ: in the state or time of shirk, before Islam
key_terms.وِلَادَتِهِ: his birth, as a basis for establishing lineage

ai.seo_question: Can captured family members inherit from one another based only on mutual acknowledgment without formal proof?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses inheritance and recognition of kinship among captives when formal proof is unavailable. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام affirms that persistent acknowledgment of a child or sibling, when made in a sound state, is sufficient for mutual inheritance. It highlights a legal basis for establishing family ties through admission even when birth occurred before Islam or outside Muslim lands.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5676 - Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Abdur Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about the hamil (the child in the womb).
Imam (as) asked: "And what is the hamil?"

I said: "A woman is captured from her land along with her young child, and she claims, 'This is my son.' Similarly, a man is captured and meets his brother, claiming, 'This is my brother,' but they have no evidence except their word."

Imam (as) then asked: "And what do the people among you say about this?"
I replied: "They do not allow inheritance unless they have proof of the child's birth, especially if the birth occurred during the period of disbelief (before Islam)."

Imam (as) said: "Glory be to Allah (swt)! If she continuously acknowledges the child as hers, and if he recognizes his brother, and both of them were sound in mind and body when making such claims, they will both remain firm in their acknowledgment, and they will inherit from one another."
